# 2026-10-23: combined source 160186731f, Perf run 40026009089. The receiver checks and FIP table add compiler source.
# Allocation baselines for the self-host compiler compiling one real module,
# checked against every run by scripts/ci-check-perf.
#
# FORMAT: metric  value  [tolerance%]. The metric key is
# <arch>/<subject>.<allocs|frees> — heap events the compiler performed while
# compiling compiler/checker.fern against internal/stdlib, counted by
# a FERN_LEAKCHECK-instrumented build (scripts/selfhost-alloc-bench).
#
# EXACT FOR A GIVEN CHECKOUT PATH, and that qualifier is the whole subtlety
# here. These count events the program performed rather than time it took,
# so on one path they repeat to the digit over every run. But the compiler
# is handed ABSOLUTE paths to the subject and the stdlib, and it allocates a
# handful FEWER for a longer one: a spread of 5 counts between a short path
# and a deeply-nested one, with GitHub's /home/runner/work/lang/lang sitting
# one BELOW /home/user/lang. That spread reproduced identically on two
# unrelated compiler binaries, so it is structural and not incidental. Four
# orders of magnitude inside the 1% tolerance, so it cannot trip the gate —
# but a local run legitimately differs from CI by a count or two, and that is
# not a regression to chase. The tolerance stays a significance threshold
# rather than a noise floor, the same as the instruction-count lanes.
#
# Quoted as a SPREAD rather than as absolute figures per path, deliberately:
# absolutes go stale every time the compiler moves, and a stale absolute reads
# as a real measurement. The pair banked below is the one GitHub's runner
# produces, since that is where the gate runs.
#
# WHY THE GAP. allocs exceeds frees by the objects live when the process exits —
# a compiler that runs once and exits does not tear its world down. The
# two are baselined separately so a change that stops freeing shows up as one
# row moving rather than being netted away.
#
# PEAK RSS IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. scripts/selfhost-alloc-bench can also read
# peak RSS out of a scratch cgroup, and that figure is not comparable across
# hosts — transparent_hugepage alone spreads the same allocation 12x — so it
# cannot be baselined against whatever runner CI hands you. The lane sets
# FERN_ALLOC_PEAK_RSS=0; peak RSS stays a local instrument, worked through in
# docs/SELFHOST-SYMBOL-INTERNING.md.
#
# x86_64 ONLY, like the append-cliff lane: the aarch64 lane does not build a
# self-host compiler. Keys stay arch-namespaced anyway, so adding that arch
# later does not renumber this one.
#
# ADVISORY AT THE TOLERANCE, FATAL AT A CEILING. The 1% above stays a
# significance threshold: a move past it is a warning, in both directions.
# perf.yml additionally sets FERN_CI_PERF_GATE_MAX_DRIFT=10 on this comparison
# alone, so drift past 10% FAILS. Two different jobs, deliberately: this pair
# sat 82% behind main for six days because a warning was the only consequence
# (#9963), while it also moves a few tenths of a percent from unrelated merges
# in a couple of hours — so a fatal 1% would fail PRs for drift they did not
# cause. When a number moves on purpose, update it in the same PR; the job
# summary prints the corrected lines ready to paste. Keep the reason in the PR,
# not here.
